title: 엘리베이터에서 만난 이웃: 몇 층 가세요?
objective: Introduce yourself to a new neighbor and ask polite -(으)세요 questions.
summary: A new resident meets a neighbor in the elevator and uses polite -(으)세요 questions.
setting: An apartment elevator. Emma moved into unit 702 this week. An older woman from unit 703 gets in.

task.title: Talk to your neighbor
task.line: Use the dialogue and word list to choose, change, fill in, order, or answer in Korean.

words.meaning: to move in (to a new home)
words.exampleMeaning: I moved to Seoul last week.

words.meaning: unit number (of an apartment or room)
to live; 사세요 is the polite question form (ㄹ drops)
polite 'Are you ...?' after a noun (instead of -이에요?)
words.exampleMeaning: Excuse me, are you a teacher?

words.meaning: Take care / Have a good one (goodbye to someone going home or inside)

dialogue.meaning: Hello. Which floor are you going to?
The 7th floor. I moved into unit 702 this week.
Oh, really? I live in unit 703.
Then we're next-door neighbors! I'm Emma. Nice to meet you.
Nice to meet you too. Are you a student, Emma?
No, I work at a company. I hope we get along well.

dialogue.korean: 저도 잘 부탁해요. 아, 7층이에요. 그럼 또 봐요.
dialogue.meaning: I hope so too. Oh, here's the 7th floor. See you again.
Okay. Take care. (said as the other person goes into their home)

exercises: Change each question to the polite -(으)세요 / -(이)세요 form: ① 어디에서 일해요? ② 회사원이에요? ③ 이 아파트에 살아요?
Fill in the blank: A: 저는 405호에 살아요. B: 아, 그래요? 만나서 ____.
Choose the right goodbye. Your neighbor is walking into her home: (a) 들어가세요 (b) 어서 오세요 (c) 잘 먹겠습니다
Put the words in order: 이사 / 저는 / 왔어요 / 지난달에
Answer in Korean. You live in unit 1102. Your neighbor asks: 몇 호에 사세요?
answers: ① 어디에서 일하세요? ② 회사원이세요? ③ 이 아파트에 사세요?
저는 지난달에 이사 왔어요. (지난달에 저는 이사 왔어요.)
